name: primary-iso3-gap
definition: For every GDACS-sourced future, whether the raw feed's top-level singular `properties.iso3` (the event's current/reporting-position country) is a member of the future's committed `iso3` array, which practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py (gdacs_futures, lines 48-50) builds only from `properties.affectedcountries`. obs-2026-08-09-1.json found six tropical-cyclone futures in both preserved GDACS snapshots (2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09) where the top-level iso3 is absent from affectedcountries and therefore absent from the future's iso3 array, even though the same country is named in the future's own `where` text. A purely mechanical field-membership check against already-preserved raw snapshot bytes — no judgement about which country is 'really' affected.
test_rule: On each nightly notary run, after gdacs_futures() extracts the night's features, for every ALERT_EPISODE future compare its committed iso3 list to the raw snapshot feature's top-level properties.iso3 for the same event id. If properties.iso3 is non-empty and not present in the future's iso3 array, record {future_id, dropped_iso3} in that night's run summary under primary_iso3_dropped. The sensor fires (is worth a note) on any run where the list is non-empty, since a coverage gap in a country field does not need a threshold or multiple nights to be a real gap — unlike sensor-fts-country-coverage, which measures a rate that needs a baseline before a change means anything.
falsification: Falsified as a live sensor once the underlying code is fixed (reading affectedcountries union the top-level iso3, or an equivalent correction) and primary_iso3_dropped stays empty for many subsequent nights purely because the bug is gone — at that point the sensor has done its one job and should be retired, not kept running for a case that can no longer occur. Also scoped, not general: NHC-sourced futures never carry affectedcountries or a comparable top-level/list split (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, nhc_futures, line 75 sets iso3 to [] unconditionally), so this sensor only ever applies to GDACS-sourced futures and would need a different check, not a wider threshold, if NHC's schema changes.

promotion.settles: a debt named by the machine's own obs-2026-08-10-2.json: the check had already run as code in every run.json since commit 79f8a02 (2026-08-09T14:50:39+00:00), with the run.py comment naming this proposal directly, but no promotion or review block had ever been written into this file.
promotion.test_rule_held: foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-12/run.json is the first run.json to exist since the fix commit (the anchor deadlock, obs-2026-08-11-1.json/obs-2026-08-12-1.json, blocked every run from 2026-08-09T14:50 until tonight) and it shows primary_iso3_dropped: [] -- exactly what the test rule expects once the six affected futures were corrected by hand (autonomy/log.jsonl step foreknown-correct-primary-iso3, 2026-08-09T14:50:39+00:00). The check ran, found nothing, and said so in the record, which is what 'held' means for a check whose own falsification clause is an eventual empty list.
promotion.kept_unchanged: definition, test_rule and falsification are the machine's text and match the running code as written; the guard still fires unconditionally on any non-empty list, no threshold added.

review.outcome: stays PROMOTED, no code change -- a new observation about the sensor's own blind spot, structural rather than about any single gap's cause: the check's return type makes it incapable of ever reporting more than one dropped country per future per night
review.why: obs-2026-09-02-1.json found that sources.primary_iso3 (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, lines 50-57) returns a set of at most one element, so run.py's `primary_iso3_dropped` computation (lines 97-116) can never name more than one missing country per future per night regardless of how many are actually missing -- a fact about the code, not about the data seen so far. Two currently-OPEN GDACS droughts show the consequence. gdacs-dr-1018332 gained 'Ireland' and 'Netherlands' in a single where/what-updating REVISED event on 2026-08-18T05:59:34+00:00; both are present in every preserved raw snapshot since (including tonight's), neither ever entered the committed iso3 array (28 entries, no IRL, no NLD), and primary_iso3_dropped has never named either across all six nights checked (2026-08-18, 19, 28, 30, 31, 09-01) because this future's singular reporting-position field has read 'ALB' or 'AUT' throughout -- both already committed. gdacs-dr-1027449 gained 'The Bahamas' and 'Cuba' in one REVISED event on 2026-08-31T11:49:28+00:00: BHS became the new primary and was correctly flagged (primary_iso3_dropped: [{future: gdacs-dr-1027449, dropped_iso3: [BHS]}] on both 2026-08-31 and 09-01), but CUB -- added by the identical event, the identical mechanism, the same night -- was never named, because it never became the primary. CUB is a clean same-night natural control: the only difference between it and the case the sensor did catch is which of the two simultaneously-added countries the feed happened to name as primary.
review.watch_for: whether IRL/NLD's now-15-night uncaught gap, and CUB's, are joined by further non-primary countries the check structurally cannot name -- every prior review already established that iso3 is not a futures.py TRACKED_FIELD and so never re-syncs (2026-08-20, 2026-08-24) and that a future leaving the feed removes it from the check's view without correcting it (2026-08-25); this review adds that even while a future stays OPEN and in view, the check can still miss a real gap whenever more than one country is added at once. This review does not widen run.py's comparison to the full affectedcountries union (which would very likely surface IRL, NLD and CUB the next time it runs, and possibly close the registry-side gap the 2026-08-20/24 reviews left open) -- that is a real change to a running, PROMOTED sensor's behaviour and is left to the maintainer, the same deferral the 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-24 reviews already made for the underlying TRACKED_FIELD question.

history.outcome: stays PROMOTED, no code change -- a new observation about the sensor's own blind spot, not about the gap's cause: closure removes a future from the check's view without correcting it
history.why: obs-2026-08-25-1.json found that gdacs-tc-1001305, the CHN case the 2026-08-24 review had just confirmed as a second standing cause, was CLOSED_BY_SOURCE tonight (foreknown/registry.json history, 2026-08-25T06:04:45+00:00) with iso3 still ['JPN'] and where still naming China -- the divergence was never corrected, only rendered permanent. primary_iso3_dropped shrank from two entries to one (gdacs-dr-1027450/ERI only) not because the CHN gap closed but because run.py's check (practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py) iterates tonight's raw GDACS feed features, and eventid 1001305 is absent from foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-25/gdacs.json's 95 features -- confirmed directly. A future that leaves the feed is exactly how futures.py already decides CLOSED_BY_SOURCE (line 231), so the check has nothing left to compare for it, ever again: a closed future cannot reopen into the feed. The list getting shorter and a gap getting fixed produce the identical run-summary signature -- the field alone cannot distinguish them.
history.watch_for: whether this is the general fate of every primary_iso3_dropped entry whose future eventually closes without the extraction being corrected -- if gdacs-dr-1027450 (still OPEN, still diverging on ERI every night since 2026-08-18) closes the same way, that would be a third instance and would make 'closes without correction, drops silently from view' the sensor's normal lifecycle for a registry-side case rather than a one-off. This review does not propose scanning CLOSED futures for a stale gap, or snapshotting a final iso3-vs-where diff into the CLOSED_BY_SOURCE event -- either would be a real fix for the blind spot, but deciding whether iso3 becomes a TRACKED_FIELD or the closure event grows a new comparison is the same design question for the registry's field model the 2026-08-20 review already left to the maintainer, not one this review settles by adding one more confirming instance.

history.outcome: stays PROMOTED, no code change -- the 2026-08-20 review's watch_for is answered: a second future, a second hazard type, the identical mechanism
history.why: obs-2026-08-24-1.json found primary_iso3_dropped's second-ever entry, gdacs-tc-1001305/CHN, first appearing tonight -- and its shape is not merely similar to gdacs-dr-1027450/ERI, it is mechanically identical: raw properties.iso3 flips from the country present at NOTARIZED (JPN) to a new one (CHN) as properties.affectedcountries grows to include it, a same-night REVISED event updates the TRACKED where field to name the new country, and the committed iso3 array -- not a TRACKED_FIELD -- stays at whatever NOTARIZED first wrote. Two independent hazard streams (drought, tropical cyclone) producing the identical three-part pattern is what the 2026-08-20 review named as the condition that would confirm a second, standing cause distinct from the original 2026-08-09 extraction bug; that condition is now met.
history.watch_for: further instances would make this the dominant cause of primary_iso3_dropped going forward (the original extraction bug's six cases were hand-corrected once, on 2026-08-09, and have not recurred since); if the count keeps growing across further hazard types and countries, the falsification clause's single-cause retirement premise ('the bug is gone, stays empty for many nights') should be read as no longer reachable by a code fix at the extraction layer, since the standing cause is registry-side, not source-side. No code change is made tonight: whether iso3 should become a TRACKED_FIELD remains a design question for the registry's field model (a REVISED event on every country-list edit is a real cost), not a bug this sensor's own scope covers, and this review does not decide it.

history.outcome: stays PROMOTED and keeps running unchanged -- the falsification clause's retirement condition ('primary_iso3_dropped stays empty for many subsequent nights purely because the bug is gone') should not be read as within reach for gdacs-dr-1027450, since a second, non-transient mechanism is now on record for the identical symptom
history.why: obs-2026-08-20-1.json found primary_iso3_dropped non-empty for the first time since the 2026-08-09 hand-correction, reporting gdacs-dr-1027450/ERI on three consecutive nights (2026-08-18, 19, 20). Unlike the six tropical-cyclone futures this sensor was written and promoted against -- where the raw feed's top-level iso3 was already absent from affectedcountries at notarization, a source-side extraction gap -- this drought's affectedcountries included ERI in every preserved raw snapshot from 2026-08-18 onward; the gap is registry-side. iso3 is not one of futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS (severity, window, what, where), so update_registry never re-syncs it once a future is notarized, even as the same night's REVISED event (2026-08-18T05:59:34+00:00) updated this future's tracked where/what to name Eritrea. The committed iso3 array therefore stays exactly as first written on 2026-08-08 for as long as this future remains OPEN, whatever the source does afterward -- a permanent divergence, not a transient one awaiting a fix of the kind obs-2026-08-09-1's cases received.
history.watch_for: whether other OPEN GDACS futures whose affectedcountries grows after notarization show the same permanent (not self-correcting) firing pattern -- that would confirm this as a second, standing cause of primary_iso3_dropped distinct from the original extraction bug, and would mean the sensor's falsification clause needs a second condition (or removal of the single-cause retirement premise) rather than a threshold change. This review does not attempt that rewrite tonight; no code change is made, since whether iso3 should become a TRACKED_FIELD (making the future's own text and country list agree, at the cost of a REVISED event on every country-list edit) is a design question for the registry's field model, not a bug this sensor's own scope covers.
